title: A retry that loads twice
prompt: Each day, `load_day` adds the day's events to the tracking table and then tells the dashboard. The dashboard is restarting, and the starter's run stops at its first timeout. Make `load_day` retry the timeouts, without changing what ends up in the table.
rules: A publish that times out (`TimeoutError`) is tried again, up to 3 attempts in all. Every day must be published.
After the run, the table holds each day's events exactly as the feed sent them: a retry never adds a day's rows twice, and events the feed sent twice stay twice.
hints: Put a retry loop around the whole body of `load_day` and run it on the sample. How many rows does 3 March have now?
A retry runs everything inside the loop again. Which part failed, and which part had already worked when it did?
Retry only the call that can time out. Or, if the whole step is retried, its write must replace the day instead of adding to it.
explanation: The step has two parts, and only the second one fails. A retry loop around both repeats the write as well, so the first day, whose publish timed out twice, is appended three times; nothing fails and nothing warns. Write once and retry only `dashboard.publish`, or make the write safe to repeat: a dynamic partition overwrite (`partitionOverwriteMode` set to `dynamic`) replaces just the day it writes, so running it three times leaves one copy. A plain `overwrite` isn't that: it replaces the whole table, so only the last day survives. Either way, the feed's own repeats are kept, because they're what the carrier sent. Before you retry a step, ask what a failed attempt already did.
